string.text: Protocol: Contour

Directive K-07. By order of Colonel George Pattonov, escort a UNISG field analyst to a suitable anomaly on the current level. Secure the site, hold the perimeter throughout the survey, and return the analyst to the issuing base with the encrypted report. Lethal force is authorized against immediate threats.

UNISG | FIELD OPERATIONS COMMAND
Directive K-07: CONTOUR
Issued by Colonel George Pattonov

Mission purpose: obtain reliable readings of spatial distortions and anomalous energy fluctuations. The data will be used to revise operational maps and identify sectors unsuitable for routine deployment.

The escort unit will deliver the field analyst to the designated anomaly, secure the survey site, and hold the perimeter until the measurement cycle is complete. Lethal force is authorized against immediate threats. Ammunition expenditure must still be entered on the appropriate form.

Once the survey is complete, bring the analyst back to the originating UNISG headquarters and submit the encrypted field package for command review.

Command note: this operation falls within acceptable risk parameters. The criteria used to determine acceptability remain classified.
The analyst has confirmed the readings and secured the encrypted field report. Assignment closed.
Biological Reconnaissance

Field Order BIO-05. Professor Nikola Teslenko requires a security escort for a UNISG biologist operating in mutant territory. Five fresh, previously unexamined carcasses must be studied on site. Kills alone do not satisfy the order. After the fifth survey, return the scientist to the original UNISG base for debriefing.

UNISG | SCIENTIFIC OPERATIONS DIVISION
Field Order BIO-05
Issued by Professor Nikola Teslenko, Director of Research

The current mutant taxonomy has been declared inadequate for operational use. Five fresh, previously unexamined carcasses are required for an on-site biological survey in active mutant habitats. Laboratory samples alone will not satisfy this requirement.

Security personnel are to escort the field biologist, maintain a safe examination perimeter, and allow the specialist to inspect each specimen personally. Authorized scientific staff will handle all collection and documentation. Lethal force is permitted against immediate threats to the expedition.

Where practical, please return specimens with the major anatomical structures intact. The Research Division notes that heads are particularly useful for identifying what has just attempted to eat you.

Following five examinations, return the specialist to the original UNISG headquarters for debriefing and sample processing. Loss of the biologist is strongly discouraged: replacement training is expensive, and the incident-report package is worse.
Five bodies examined and the biological report secured. The field assignment is complete.
You are the analyst assigned to the anomaly survey?
Yes. Keep my name off the open channel. I have a calibrated probe and an anomaly the Directorate wants mapped.
What do you need from me?
A clear approach and a quiet perimeter. One stray bullet can ruin the readings. Once I start the scan, stay close until the data series is complete.
Understood. I will secure the route.
Then we move. Your orders come from the same people as mine.
We are back at headquarters. Is the survey package ready for command?
Ready and encrypted. The anomaly shifted twice during the run, so I included the unprocessed readings as well as the final analysis.
Transmit it over the secure channel. That concludes the escort assignment.
Transfer confirmed, mission closed, payment authorized. Colonel Pattonov also wants an ammunition report, including if you used none.
You are the biologist? I was told you needed protection.
Protection, yes. And patience. Command wants field observations, not bags of mutant parts with no context.
How many samples are we talking about?
Five fresh bodies. Put the mutants down, then give me room to examine them. If I cannot reach a specimen, it does not count.
I will keep them off you. Do not wander off.
Agreed. Five examinations and we both get to go home. Preferably with all our limbs.
We made it back. Have all five samples been logged?
Every one of them. Two specimens already challenge our existing classification. Professor Teslenko will finally have something worth reading.
File the report with Research. My security detail is standing down.
Report filed, escort released, payment confirmed. I even get to put a zero on the personnel-loss form. Administration loves a clean form.
Field survey complete: five of five samples. Escort the biologist back to the original UNISG base and speak with him to submit the report.
Faction: UNISG\nLocation: Exclusion Zone, anomalous sectors
